title: Vanishing of the first cohomology of the successive kernels after twisting
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense of Stacks Properties Definition 01PS [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] (since $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is affine, this is the same as $\mathcal L$ being $f$-ample, Stacks Morphisms Lemma 01VK; write $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ for the $d$-fold tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]). Let $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the ideal sheaf generated by $I$, i.e. the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to f^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], [def-pc-module-pullback], where $\widetilde I\subseteq\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ is the quasi-coherent ideal associated with $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and put $\mathcal F_0=0$. Then there is an integer $d_0$ such that $H^1(X,\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $n\ge0$ and every $d\ge d_0$, where $H^1$ is sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0884 (lemma-vanishing-projective); proof via Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness), and Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample)

proof.text: *$X$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal, so $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is defined.* $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is covered by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian, so it is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and it is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii); hence it is a Noetherian scheme. A proper morphism is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1), applied to $f$ and $\mathcal J=\widetilde I$ (a quasi-coherent ideal with $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde I)=I$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]), $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal I(U)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ generated by $f^\sharp(I)$. So $X$ and $\mathcal I$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0884 (lemma-vanishing-projective), hypotheses; Morphisms Lemma 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Properties Definition 01OV

proof.text: *The graded algebra $B$.* Put $B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B_n$, $B_n=I^n/I^{n+1}$ ($I^0=A$), a commutative graded $A$-algebra with multiplication induced by that of $A$. Since $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I=(x_1,\dots,x_r)$; $B_0=A/I$ is a quotient of $A$ and $B_n$ is spanned over $A$ by the classes of the monomials of degree $n$ in the $x_i$, so $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the classes $\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_r\in B_1$: $B$ is a finitely generated graded $A$-algebra.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0884 (lemma-vanishing-projective), first sentence ('Set B = \bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}')

proof.text: *A surjection of graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\psi:f^*\widetilde B\to\mathcal A:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$.* (Stacks writes $\mathcal A=f^*\widetilde B$; this equality fails in general, e.g. for $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ one has $\mathcal I=0$ while $f^*\widetilde{B_1}=\widetilde{I/I^2}\neq0$ when $I\neq I^2$; only the surjection is needed.) Let $\widetilde B=\bigoplus_n\widetilde{B_n}$ be the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-algebra associated with $B$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module] (on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\Gamma=A$). For each $n$ the map $\varphi_n:B_n\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1})$, $a\bmod I^{n+1}\mapsto f^\sharp(a)\bmod\mathcal I^{n+1}$, is well defined and $A$-linear: by Step 1 $f^\sharp(I)$ lands in $\mathcal I(U)$ on every affine $U$, so $f^\sharp(I^k)\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^k)$ (powers as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)). By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-hom] and the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $\varphi_n$ corresponds to a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\psi_n:f^*\widetilde{B_n}\to\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ with $\psi_n(f^*c(b))=\varphi_n(b)$ for the canonical sections $c(b)$, $b\in B_n$; put $\psi=\bigoplus_n\psi_n$. On an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $C=\mathcal O_X(U)$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies $(f^*\widetilde{B_n})(U)=B_n\otimes_AC$, and $\psi$ becomes $\bar a\otimes c\mapsto c\,f^\sharp(a)\bmod\mathcal I^{n+1}$; this is multiplicative, $(\bar a\otimes c)(\bar a'\otimes c')=\overline{aa'}\otimes cc'\mapsto cc'f^\sharp(aa')$, so $\psi$ is a morphism of sheaves of graded algebras. It is an epimorphism: a local section of $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ lifts locally to a section of $\mathcal I^n$, which locally on affines $U$ is a sum of products of $n$ sections of $\mathcal I(U)=f^\sharp(I)C$ (Step 1), i.e. of the form $\sum_jc_jf^\sharp(a_j)$ with $a_j\in I^n$, the image of $\sum_j\bar a_j\otimes c_j$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0884 (lemma-vanishing-projective) ('\mathcal B = \bigoplus \mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1} = f^*\widetilde B', corrected to a surjection); cf. the computation in the proof of Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback)

proof.text: *The kernels form a finite type graded $f^*\widetilde B$-module.* Put $\mathcal K_n=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)$ ($n\ge0$, so $\mathcal K_0=\mathcal F_1$) and $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal K_n$. By Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-kernel-rees-finite], $\mathcal G$ is a finite type graded quasi-coherent module over $\mathcal A=\bigoplus\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$. Through the surjection $\psi$ of Step 3, $\mathcal G$ is a graded quasi-coherent $f^*\widetilde B$-module, and it is of finite type over $f^*\widetilde B$: local homogeneous generators over $\mathcal A$ remain generators over $f^*\widetilde B$, since every local section of $\mathcal A$ is locally the image of a local section of $f^*\widetilde B$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0884, using Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra)

proof.text: *Uniform vanishing.* By Step 2, $B$ is a finitely generated graded $A$-algebra; $A$ is Noetherian, $f$ is proper, $\mathcal G$ is a finite type graded quasi-coherent $f^*\widetilde B$-module (Step 4) and $\mathcal L$ is ample in the sense of Stacks 01PS [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], which is the ampleness hypothesis of Stacks Lemma 0897 (2). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-graded-vanishing] gives $d_0$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=0$ for all $d\ge d_0$. (That node's statement currently cites def-sc-ample; its source, Stacks 0897 (2), uses the absolute notion 01PS, as here.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0884 ('Hence the lemma follows from Lemma 0897 part (2)'); Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness) (2)

proof.text: *Passing to each summand.* For each $n$ the inclusion $\iota_n:\mathcal K_n\to\mathcal G$ and the projection $\pi_n:\mathcal G\to\mathcal K_n$ satisfy $\pi_n\iota_n=\mathrm{id}$; tensoring with $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (a functor) keeps $(\pi_n\otimes1)(\iota_n\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}$, and applying the functor $H^1(X,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] shows that $H^1(X,\mathcal K_n\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ is a retract of $H^1(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=0$ for $d\ge d_0$ (Step 5). So $H^1(X,\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=0$ for all $n\ge0$ and $d\ge d_0$.

The splitter of this node should restate ampleness through that node so that lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation applies.
